findings.title: forceError claimed, not tested
findings.detail: Header says a prior review failed a forceError-in-browser claim and that 'this is that claim turned into a test'. The suite only covers empty-submit policies and a happy-path ask (describe 'useAssistantPanel — empty submit'). No forceError path, flag, or case appears anywhere in the 167 lines. Author narrative and artifact disagree.

findings.title: ignore test can false-pass
findings.detail: submit uses optional chaining: await latest?.submit(event). If latest is still null, submit is a silent no-op. The 'ignore' case then still passes: asked stays 0, error and answer stay null — the same as never invoking the hook. That makes the ignore assertions compatible with a failed mount/submit race, so the check can pass without proving onEmptySubmit: 'ignore'. Send/happy-path cases fail harder on expected side effects; ignore does not.

findings.title: Browser lane execution not verified
findings.detail: File is named .browser.test.ts and comments assert it runs under pet-sitter's @vitest/browser + chromium lane. The diff adds only this file: no vitest config, no include pattern, no run output. From the diff alone it is impossible to verify the file is discovered or executed in a real browser, so the 'real DOM / browser lane' claim does not pass.

findings.title: Hook behavior unproven by this diff
findings.detail: Tests import useAssistantPanel from design-system/hooks/useAssistantPanel but the hook implementation is not in the diff. Assertions (empty POST still fires under send, answer forced null with EMPTY, API error preferred over emptyMessage, trim of answer, links from selectItems) encode expected behavior that cannot be confirmed here. Adding a test file is not proof the shared hook implements those policies.

findings.title: No sushi-finder artifact in commit
findings.detail: Reviewed commit only introduces a pet-sitter test. Zero sushi-finder source, route, acceptance, or screenshot changes appear. Any sushi-finder product claim for this commit is unsupported by the diff.
